subject: psychiatry
title: Neurodevelopmental disorders

steps.tx: Children with **autism spectrum disorder** show persistent difficulty with **social communication** together with restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour from early life. The social difficulty affects reciprocity, nonverbal communication and relationships with other children. The repetitive pattern includes stereotyped movements, insistence on sameness, fixated interests and unusual sensory responses. Clinicians specify language ability and intellectual ability separately because both vary widely. Girls often camouflage their difficulties and therefore receive a later diagnosis.
steps.say: Children with autism spectrum disorder have persistent difficulty with social communication from early childhood. They also show restricted and repetitive behaviour that includes stereotyped movements and fixated interests. Clinicians describe language ability and intellectual ability separately because each child differs considerably. Girls often camouflage their social difficulty, and this pattern causes a fairly later diagnosis in many cases.

steps.tx: Children with **ADHD** show pervasive inattention or hyperactivity and impulsivity that starts before twelve years and impairs function across settings. Teachers and parents must provide evidence from school and home because a single setting is not enough. Affected children lose things, struggle with organisation, fidget frequently, talk excessively and interrupt others during conversation. **Stimulants** remain first line treatment for moderate to severe disease when prescribing includes regular monitoring. Clinicians check pulse, blood pressure, weight, height and cardiac family history before treatment starts.
steps.say: Children with ADHD show inattention or hyperactivity that starts before twelve years and affects two settings. Parents and teachers provide important evidence because symptoms must appear at home and school. Stimulants remain first line treatment for moderate to severe disease in many children. Clinicians check pulse, blood pressure, weight, height and cardiac history before treatment starts.

steps.tx: People with **intellectual disability** have deficits in intellectual functioning and adaptive functioning that begin during the developmental period. Severity depends on adaptive support needs rather than intelligence quotient alone because daily function matters most clinically. Causes include Down syndrome, fragile X syndrome, fetal alcohol exposure and acquired brain insults after birth. Clinicians search for the underlying cause and treat comorbid epilepsy, autism and mental illness carefully. **Diagnostic overshadowing** occurs when clinicians wrongly attribute every new symptom to the disability itself.
steps.say: People with intellectual disability have impaired intellectual functioning and impaired adaptive functioning from childhood onward. Clinicians grade severity by support needs because daily function matters more than scores alone. Causes include Down syndrome, fragile X syndrome and fetal alcohol exposure before birth. Clinicians search for treatable comorbidity and avoid attributing every symptom to disability itself.

steps.tx: Motor disorders include developmental coordination disorder, stereotyped movements and **tic disorders** that impair daily life for affected children. **Tourette syndrome** requires multiple motor tics plus at least one vocal tic for over one year. Tics start before eighteen years, wax and wane over time and remain briefly suppressible after a premonitory urge. **Habit reversal training** is first line treatment for impairing tics because it teaches a competing response. Most childhood tics are transient and need clear explanation rather than medication.
steps.say: Tourette syndrome requires multiple motor tics and one vocal tic for over one year. Tics start before eighteen years and wax and wane over many months. Children can suppress tics briefly after feeling a strong premonitory urge beforehand. Habit reversal training is first line treatment because it teaches safer competing responses.

steps.tx: This image shows a schoolboy in a classroom with labels pointing to multiple motor movements and one vocal sound. The labels remind students that **Tourette syndrome** needs multiple motor tics plus at least one vocal tic over a year. The classroom setting matters because tics often become visible during school and cause embarrassment for children. **Premonitory urge** and brief suppressibility help separate tics from other abnormal movements in examinations.
steps.say: This image presents a schoolboy in a classroom with labels for motor and vocal tics. The picture is useful because Tourette syndrome is characterised by multiple motor tics with one vocal tic. Tics often become noticeable during school and cause embarrassment for affected children. A premonitory urge with brief suppressibility helps clinicians distinguish tics from other movements.
